data.narrative: Designed and hardened the Core API for the URL shortener: chose a prefixed redirect style (/r/<code>) to keep the public redirect namespace separate from the admin API, built strict URL validation (http/https allowlist, control-character rejection, userinfo rejection) wired to a 400 error contract, and implemented create/list/get endpoints backed by the Postgres layer from Module 2. Closed a full break/fix loop: an injected userinfo bypass (https://good.com@evil.example.com) stored and served a live open redirect (302 to the attacker host), then fixed at validation time, purged the persisted bad row, and locked in with 15 pytest regression tests plus a live abuse suite. Checkpoint demo confirmed create 201, redirect 302 with correct Location header, inspect 200, and fail-closed 404 on unknown codes.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose prefix_r over a top-level /:code route, reasoning that a dedicated /r namespace avoids route collisions with app endpoints and separates the untrusted public hot path from the admin API.
dimension_scores.evidence: DECIDE recorded via upsk decide with reasoning 'no route collisions, /r namespace separates public redirect from app routes'.

dimension_scores.observation: Closed the BREAK loop end to end: reproduced the open-redirect exploit live (stored 201, redirect 302 to attacker host), root-caused it to a missing userinfo check in the allowlist, fixed validation, purged the compromised row, and added 15 regression tests covering all abuse variants.
dimension_scores.evidence: pytest: 15 passed; /r/ll1J70 returns 404 after purge; live abuse suite shows 10 variants rejected 400.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified open redirect as the worst-case phishing/credential-harvesting vector for a public link shortener, blocked the userinfo trick that naive allowlists miss, rejects control characters and non-http(s) schemes, and ensures nothing bad is persisted.
dimension_scores.evidence: https://good.com@evil.example.com -> 400; ftp:/javascript:/data: -> 400; zero compromised URLs remain in DB.

dimension_scores.observation: Distinguished the public redirect (minimal, trust-boundary, hot path) from the admin API; made validation errors a consistent 400 'nothing stored' contract; fail-closed expiry so expired and never-existed codes are indistinguishable to attackers.
dimension_scores.evidence: Checkpoint demo: 'redirect separate from admin API' and 'expired 404 indistinguishable from never-existed (fail closed)'.

dimension_scores.observation: Stated precisely what was proved (validation boundary holds, abuse suite clean, tests green) versus what risk remains (no auth or rate limiting yet) in a two-sentence checkpoint demo.
dimension_scores.evidence: Checkpoint demo narrative covers proven behavior plus remaining risk.

strengths: Route design justified by collision and trust-boundary reasoning, not convention.
Open-redirect vector found and fixed with a persisted-row purge plus 15 regression tests, not just a validation patch.
Fail-closed 404 semantics so attackers cannot distinguish expired links from nonexistent ones.
Consistent 400 error contract: rejected input is never stored.
data.recommendation: Next module: add authentication and authorization so link creation and enumeration are scoped to a caller, plus rate limiting on the public redirect path.
